deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a 'système de pseudo-droites' with n lines is drawn in a disk D, which serves as a model of the affine plane. Each pseudo-line meets the boundary circle in two points, so the 2n endpoints form a combinatorial polygon S of order 2n. S carries a free involution ±1_S exchanging the two ends of each line, and I_0 = S/{±1_S} is the n-element set of lines. 'Stable' means simple: no three lines concurrent, and any two lines cross exactly once.

The objects defined on the page:
- C̃_st(S) is the set of isotopy classes of stable systems with the boundary pinned by S.
- The dihedral group D_S = Aut(S) has order 4n and acts on C̃_st(S), functorially in S.
- The quotient C̃_st(S)/D_S is C_aff,st(n), the set of isomorphism classes of stable systems (X,Σ,Δ).
- The stabilizer of a class ξ̃ in D_S equals the group Aut_isot(D,Σ̃) computed in the isotopy category, which is Aut(X,Σ,Δ).
- Orbit–stabilizer gives |orbit of ξ̃| = 4n/N(ξ), where N(ξ) = |Aut(X,Σ,Δ)|. The previous page derived this through the degree-2 map to C^!_diffst(I_0).
- Quotienting only by the antipody {±1_S} gives C_Hst(I_0), which Grothendieck notes is contained in C_aff,st(I_0).

Worked examples:
- n=3: there is one class, with Aut ≅ S_3, so |C̃_st(S)| = 12/6 = 2. These are the two orientations of the central triangle.
- n=4: there is one class, with Aut ≅ Z/2, so |C̃_st(S)| = 16/2 = 8.
- n=5: there are 6 classes; the computation is left unfinished.

In modern terms, C̃_st(S) is in bijection with:
- rhombic (zonotopal) tilings of the regular 2n-gon;
- equivalently, commutation classes of reduced words for the longest element w_0 of S_n.
Their counts are 1, 1, 2, 8, 62, 908, ...

C_aff,st(n) is the set of simple Euclidean (affine) pseudoline arrangements up to isomorphism. The n=4 case matches the unique simple arrangement of 5 lines in RP^2: its symmetry group is D_5 of order 10 and acts transitively on the lines, so the stabilizer of the line at infinity is Z/2.
errors: No errors found. 2 and 8 are correct counts of rhombic tilings of the hexagon and octagon.

For n=5, Grothendieck's value card = 6 is consistent with the known 62 tilings of the decagon, for example via 62 = 20+20+10+5+5+2, i.e. automorphism orders 1,1,2,4,4,10. However, this decomposition was not verified here.
The last line, C̃_st(S)/{±1_S} ≅ C_Hst(I_0), is only sketched. The meaning of 'H' is unclear, and the inclusion into C_aff,st(I_0) is merely asserted with an exclamation mark.

ideas.what: Pinned (boundary-labelled) simple pseudoline arrangements in a disk, with the dihedral group of the 2n-gon acting on them
ideas.modern_name: Wiring diagrams / rhombic tilings of the 2n-gon / commutation classes of reduced words of w_0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (wiring diagrams, 1980), Stanley (1984), Elnitsky (1997), Knuth (Axioms and Hulls, 1992)

ideas.what: Orbit–stabilizer count |orbit| = 4n/|Aut(X,Σ,Δ)|, with the stabilizer identified with the automorphism group in the isotopy category
ideas.modern_name: Orbit counting / Burnside for arrangements up to symmetry

ideas.what: Small-case enumeration: n=3 gives 1 class (Aut S_3) and 2 pinned classes; n=4 gives 1 class (Aut Z/2) and 8 pinned classes; n=5 gives 6 classes
ideas.modern_name: Enumeration of simple Euclidean pseudoline arrangements

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine orbit counts of simple pseudoline arrangements. They are well known in the literature as rhombic tilings and reduced-word commutation classes. The only point of interest is Grothendieck's framing via 'isotopic categories' and pinned disks, which is not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The page number '5)' at top-left is probably a sheet/section numeral rather than part of the item numbering. The items are '2) n=4' and '3) n=5'.
'card C_aff(n)' is written in the image like 'C_{·ff}(n)'. The previous page uses 'C_{·diff}'. The subscript is ambiguous; on this page it is resolved as 'C_{aff,st}' in the Résumé.
The struck word after 'D_S' is a crossed-out 'calculé' (or similar), followed by 'On a'.
'8t' / '8r' in the handwriting is 'st' (stable). The subscript of C̃ should read 'st' throughout.
In the last line the boxed insertion reads '⊂ C_{aff,st}(I_0)'. The subscript under H appears to be 'st', with a crossed-out 'ce' beneath.
